assessment.answer: The score is high because the 8 inputs show a tiny, shrinking company: total liabilities of $30.0M against only $3.4M of assets (8.9x versus a peer median of 0.59x), a current ratio of 0.07, and an annualized net loss of $16.2M, which is -483% of assets and in the bottom 4% of peers. The filings confirm this is real distress and not an artefact. Cash was only $109,692 (0.23 months of burn), and since the quarter ended the company has been hit by a series of defaults and accelerations from Agile, AFG, ASCAP, Cara, Balboa, the May 2023 secured lenders, 1800 Diagonal and the Bellino Trust, together several million dollars that its cash cannot cover.
moved_by: Secured lender Agile called a default on July 21, 2025 and accelerated $1,000,476, payable within seven days, with rights to the collateral
The May 2023 Secured Line of Credit, secured by all assets, was not repaid at its May 10, 2025 maturity ($889,000 owed), and the default is uncured
Further accelerations and final demands in July-August 2025: ASCAP $1,175,000, Cara Communications $361,800, AFG $268,035, Balboa $82,427, and 1800 Diagonal $286,326 at 150%
Missed June 1, 2025 payment and declared default on the $2.0M, 30% Bellino Trust note
Cash of $109,692 at June 30, 2025 (0.23 months of cash) against roughly $4M of accelerated non-insider claims
Not in compliance with financial covenants on most equipment financings at June 30, 2025
Lender converting defaulted debt into stock at $0.001353 per share, a share price near zero, so raising equity is effectively closed
Partly offsetting: the Executive Chairman took over the defaulted Bellino note and keeps funding the company through Excel
